mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressures that may lead to tighter monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the inflation signal, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL and SPX returns over a 3-year rolling window is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over the past 6 months indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the demand signal, or if RSAFS growth is not significantly correlated with SPX returns over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased costs for businesses, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the labor market signal, or if UNRATE changes are not significantly correlated with SPX returns over a 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the past 3 months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the supply contraction signal, or if INDPRO changes are not significantly correlated with SPX returns over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 2% annualized, the combination signals a mismatch between monetary policy and inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the mismatch signal, or if the interaction of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL is not significantly correlated with SPX returns over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased costs for businesses, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the labor market signal, or if the interaction of PAYEMS and UNRATE is not significantly correlated with SPX returns over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) over the past 6 months indicates strengthening demand in the housing market, which boosts related sectors and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the housing demand signal, or if HOUST growth is not significantly correlated with SPX returns over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) combined with an increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) signals a supply-demand imbalance, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the supply-demand imbalance signal, or if the interaction of INDPRO and RSAFS is not significantly correlated with SPX returns over a 3-year rolling window.
